conference.detail: Business visits such as meetings and conferences fit the waiver.

unpaid-speaking.detail: Speaking at a conference without payment is generally a business visit; officers decide at the border.
unpaid-speaking.next: Carry the invitation showing no payment beyond expenses.

paid-speaking.route: Guam-CNMI visa waiver or ESTA (honorarium rules)
paid-speaking.detail: Speaking fees are allowed only from qualifying (mainly academic or nonprofit research) institutions, for no more than nine days at one institution and from no more than five institutions in six months; no salary from a US entity.
paid-speaking.next: Check the payer qualifies; otherwise a work visa is needed.

book-launch.route: Guam-CNMI visa waiver or ESTA or a work visa
book-launch.detail: Promotion and readings may be business activity; paid appearances fall under the honorarium limits.
book-launch.next: Ask a US Embassy or an immigration lawyer.

ai-teaching.route: Guam-CNMI visa waiver or ESTA (honorarium rules) or a work visa
ai-teaching.detail: Academic lectures can fit the honorarium rules; paid teaching for a company needs a work visa.

remote-work.route: Not addressed for visitors (US immigration law)
remote-work.detail: Visitors (ESTA or B visa) may not take employment; the State Department pages list meetings, conferences and negotiations but do not address remote work for a foreign employer either way.
remote-work.next: Ask US Customs and Border Protection or a US consulate in writing.

laws.rule: Drug penalties are severe and can include mandatory minimum sentences. Possessing 1 ounce or less of cannabis is legal under Guam law but illegal under US federal law. Some medicines legal in Australia are controlled in the US; possessing prescription medicine without a prescription is illegal.
Buying, selling or owning counterfeit or pirated goods is illegal.

visa-preparation.entry_summary: US territory: enter under US rules (ESTA and Visa Waiver Program, or the Guam-CNMI Visa Waiver Program for direct stays under 45 days), plus Guam's electronic declaration.
visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Guam-CNMI Visa Waiver Program for a direct trip under 45 days, or ESTA for up to 90 days.

steps.step: Complete Guam's mandatory electronic declaration form (opens 72 hours before departure).
If you'll only visit Guam or the CNMI for under 45 days, you may enter under the G-CNMI Visa Waiver Program; otherwise get an ESTA (up to 90 days) or a US visa.
